title: Architecture Trade-offs
description: Evaluate real-world architecture decisions through structured trade-off analysis. Each problem presents competing approaches and asks you to justify the right choice for a given context.

data.text: Architecture is the art of balancing competing constraints. Speed versus flexibility. Consistency versus availability. Simplicity versus scalability. Every senior engineer is expected to articulate why they chose one path over another, not just what they built.

data.title: Core competencies
items: Evaluate competing architectural approaches using structured criteria
Communicate trade-offs clearly to stakeholders and engineering teams
Recognize when a popular pattern is the wrong pattern for your context
Apply CAP theorem, bounded contexts, and saga patterns to real decisions
Balance short-term delivery velocity against long-term operational cost

data.title: How to use this module
data.text: Treat each problem as an interview-style prompt. State your assumptions, enumerate trade-offs, justify your recommendation, and name the risks. There is rarely one right answer—there is only a well-reasoned answer.

These ten problems cover the most common architecture decision points that surface in senior and staff-level interviews. They are drawn from real production incidents, design reviews, and post-mortems. Each lesson includes a recommended solution, but the value is in understanding the reasoning—not memorizing the answer.

terms.definition: A decision where gaining one quality causes losing another.
A boundary within which a domain model is consistent and valid.
A distributed system can provide at most two of: Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.

furtherReading.title: The Architecture of Open Source Applications

longDescription: Master architecture decision-making through ten realistic problems. Compare modular monoliths against microservices, evaluate API styles, choose data stores for specific workload patterns, and decide when a distributed workflow needs orchestration versus choreography. Each lesson provides structured trade-off analysis, recommended solutions, and the reasoning behind them.
